newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen Central Bank gives treasury bill results.
newsitem.headline: Yemen Central Bank gives treasury bill results.

text.p: The Central Bank of Yemen said on Sunday its latest issue of 91-day treasury bills yielded an average 19.47 percent, down from the average 19.88 percent at the March 5 auction.
Of the 1.8 billion rials worth of bills on offer the issue attracted subscriptions worth 1.746 billion rials.
The average price was 9,537 rials and the lowest price accepted was 9,521.14 rials. Yields ranged from 16.5 percent to 20.17 percent.

The latest issue of 182-day bills yielded an average 20.97 percent, from 21.41 percent at the March 5 auction. Of the 800 million rials worth of 182-day bills on offer, the issue attracted subscriptions worth 776 million rials.
The average price was 9,035.31 rials and the lowest price accepted was 9,021.75 rials. Yields ranged from 18.16 percent to 21.50 percent.
The latest issue of 364-day bills yielded an average of 20.71 percent from the March 5 average of 22.15 percent.
Of the 400 million rials worth of the 364-day bills on offer, the issue attracted subscriptions worth 388 million rials.
The average price was 8,288.55 rials and the lowest price accepted was 8,201.14.
Yields ranged from 18.51 percent to 22 percent.
The Bank did not fix a date for the next auction. But a Bank official told Reuters that the bank "has decided recently to hold the auction twice a month".
